title: The training intensity distribution among well-trained and elite endurance athletes
claims: The majority of retrospective analyses of nationally and internationally competitive endurance athletes present a pyramidal training intensity distribution with a high proportion of high-volume, low-intensity training.
Some world-class athletes adopt a polarized distribution with a significant share of high-volume, low-intensity training and high-intensity training during certain phases of the season.
Polarized training is commonly defined as about 75-80% low intensity, about 5% threshold intensity and about 15-20% high intensity.
Reported low-intensity shares across endurance disciplines range from roughly 70% to 96%, including runners, cross-country skiers, rowers, cyclists and swimmers.

Emerging prospective randomized controlled studies have demonstrated superior endurance-related responses with polarized training compared with high-volume low-intensity or threshold-focused training in well-trained and recreational individuals.

摘要：部分世界级运动员在赛季特定阶段采用极化分布。
正文：极化常量化为 75–80% 低强度、5% 阈值、15–20% 高强度。
正文表格与综述：低强度占比约 70%–96%，覆盖跑、越野滑雪、赛艇、自行车、游泳。
摘要：新兴前瞻 RCT 显示，极化在耐力相关指标上优于高量低强度或阈值训练。
